name: Market Hall

text: The roof is one span of iron and glass and you cannot see both ends of it
from anywhere in the building.
A card by the door: 412 STALLS. LET WEEKLY. THERE IS A WAITING LIST.
Fish, on ice brought down from the north by rail overnight.
The board lists nine kinds and has three of them crossed out.
Under the crossings, in the same chalk: NOT COMING IN. ASK THE BOATS WHY.
Bread in twelve shapes, and a queue that has learned to fold itself
so as not to block the aisle.
The city eats about nine tons of this a day. Somebody worked it out and put it up.
Cloth by the bolt, from four regions, and a girl measuring against her arm
because the yardstick has been borrowed and not returned.
She is faster than the yardstick and everybody knows it.
Charms, luck knots, and small carved things for the mantelpiece.
Half the stall is spirals. A card claims they are Aurelian.
They are not, and the woman selling them will tell you so if you ask.
Feed, grit and bedding, by the sack, with a scale that is checked monthly
and a certificate to prove it hanging over the scale.
Aureline is very serious about weights and about almost nothing else.
Ironmongery. Everything hangs from a beam and the whole stall rings
when a cart goes past outside.
The stallholder has stopped hearing it. Nobody else has.
Herbs, dried, in jars, with the price and the ailment on each label.
A separate shelf is labelled DOES NOT WORK BUT PEOPLE LIKE IT,
and is the busiest shelf on the stall.
Imports off the quays. Shell money, a jar of something in oil,
and a rolled chart of a coast that is not on any map you have seen.
The label says SUNDER ISLES. NINE WEEKS BY SEA. NOT THE FAR SIDE.

_plan: Four hundred and twelve stalls, sixteen of them drawn, and a roof you cannot see the ends of. Nothing here is about the player at all, which is the point: this is the room that proves Aureline was here before them and will be here after. The only Act 4 material is a fish board with three lines chalked out and ASK THE BOATS WHY, which is the deep-water fleet being bought up, seen from the wrong end.
